page2_img_2.png.title: Gerrit JSON snippet for review 41591
page2_img_2.png.description: A screenshot of the Gerrit JSON response for change id 41591 showing nested fields used to describe patch set metadata. The top shows currentPatchSetId referencing changeId: 41591 and patchSetId: 2, and a patchSets array containing an entry for patchSetId: 1 with a revision id (beginning 23e32e...) and createdOn timestamp "2012-08-17 03:20:48.036000000" (draft: false). A messages array (with a UUID like AAAI6X///9M=) and an empty dependsOn list are visible, illustrating the deep, repetitive structure the authors parsed to extract patchSetId, revision, timestamps, and other review details.

page3_img_1.png.title: Monthly counts of Android Gerrit reviews (2008–2013)
page3_img_1.png.description: A time-series line chart of monthly "Reviews per Month" (y-axis) plotted against time from 2008 through early 2013 (x-axis). The plot shows a general rise in review activity from low tens/hundreds per month in 2008 to a first peak around 2010 (roughly 700–900 reviews/month), a subsequent decline into 2011, a pronounced gap near zero between mid‑2011 and the start of 2012, and then a recovery with a larger peak in 2012 (approximately 1,200–1,300 reviews/month) before falling again toward the end of 2012 and rising into 2013. The paper notes the near‑zero period corresponds to Gerrit database cleanups that removed stalled reviews, explaining the missing data seen in the plot.

page4_img_1.png.title: Relational schema for Gerrit Android code-review dataset
page4_img_1.png.description: An entity-relationship diagram showing the relational schema used to store Gerrit review data. Central is the Review table (ReviewId primary key) with fields such as OwnerId, Message, Subject, CreatedOn, LastUpdatedOn, Project, Branch, SubmitType, and Status; it links to PatchSet (PatchSetId, PatchSetNumber, NumberOfFiles, CreatedOn, GitRevision) and to Approval, Comment, and Person tables. The Person table (PersonId primary key) includes Name, Email and IsBotAccount and is referenced by Review, Approval and Comment; Approval entries are identified by the composite key (ReviewId, PersonId) and store ReviewedStatus/When and VerifiedStatus/When. PatchSetFile (PatchSetFileId key) records per-file details (Path, ChangeType, LinesAdded, LinesDeleted) and Comment records include associations to ReviewId, PatchSetId, PatchSetFileId plus CommentId, Message, WrittenOn, AuthorId, Path, LineNumber and Side.

page2_img_1.png.title: Gerrit review page showing metadata, reviewers, patch sets, diffs, and comments
page2_img_1.png.description: Screenshot of an Android Gerrit review (change 41591) showing the change header (Change-Id, Owner: Shuo Gao, Project: platform/frameworks/base, Branch: master), timestamps (Uploaded Aug 16, 2012; Updated Feb 6, 2013) and a commit message describing a null‑dereference fix. A reviewer table shows approvals and verifications (Deckard Autoverifier with a Verified check, Jeffrey Brown with a negative mark, Christophe Bransiec +1, Bruce Beare +1, etc.). The middle pane shows Patch Set 2 details (Author: Christophe Bransiec; Committer: Shuo Gao), a file listing for core/java/.../SQLiteQueryBuilder.java with two inline comments and a +1/−1 diff. The threaded comments area below records automated and manual verifications (Jean‑Baptiste Queru, Deckard Autoverifier), individual reviewer votes (e.g., Jeffrey Brown’s Code‑Review -2) and discussion text (Jeffrey Brown argues for throwing IllegalArgumentException rather than returning null), illustrating multi‑patch iteration and reviewer feedback.

page4_img_2.png.title: Weekday boxplots of number of Android code reviews (late 2012)
page4_img_2.png.description: Seven side-by-side boxplots show the distribution of code reviews submitted on each day of the week (Sun through Sat) for the last half of 2012. The vertical axis is labeled “Reviews” (scale to about 175) and each boxplot shows median, interquartile range, whiskers, and outliers; weekdays (Mon–Fri) have substantially higher medians and wider IQRs than weekend days. There are several high outliers on mid-week days (points approaching ~150–175 reviews), while Sunday shows almost no activity and Saturday sits between the two. The paper reports t-test results confirming no significant differences among Monday–Friday but statistically higher submission counts on weekdays than on Saturday and Sunday, with Saturday also significantly higher than Sunday.
